design.affected_system: heat-health surveillance, prevention, and care coordination
alternatives: activate a bounded reserve from forecast risk bands for daily heat-health care and outreach demand
use rolling forecasts and conservative capacity triggers for daily heat-health care and outreach demand
pair lag-aware heat-health workload forecasting with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Health records are privacy-preserving, population-defined, timely, and separated from service-request proxies.
Heat exposure, care seeking, reporting, and intervention effects remain distinct constructs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: continue ordinary capacity planning for daily heat-health care and outreach demand.

constraints.description: The heat-health surveillance and prevention forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: public-health preparedness director and emergency medical services lead
design.decision_question: What probabilistic emergency, call-center, and outreach workload should health operations prepare for?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The heat-health surveillance and prevention forecast must respect declared validated operational capacity and forecast uncertainty.
independence_key.decision_object: daily heat-health care and outreach demand
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for daily heat-health care and outreach demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

design.intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting daily heat-health care and outreach demand, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in health-response demand above staffed capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present forecast encounters as illnesses, admissions, or deaths.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for daily heat-health care and outreach demand passes documented checks for held-out error, interval coverage, event detection, drift, and baseline comparison.

design.title: Forecast heat-related care and outreach demand
transportability_risks: Clinical coding, surveillance coverage, acclimatization, housing, and care access vary.
Small-area health estimates may be unstable or disclosure-sensitive.

family.affected_system: heat-health surveillance, prevention, and care coordination
claim_boundary: Area exposure, service, and vulnerability records do not diagnose individuals or prove harm.
Operational allocations are proposed planning outputs, not delivered clinical or social services.
Health-effect claims require outcome panels, identification, privacy, and external review.
family.decision_owner: public-health preparedness director and emergency medical services lead
family.description: Eight health-centered decisions for syndrome diagnosis, demand forecasting, prevention investment, care access, outreach allocation, surveillance timing, surge stress, and evaluation.
family.title: Heat-health surveillance and prevention

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
